query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: A well-graded crew-service axis directly tied to the query on service improvement and recommendation drivers; strong grouping leverage. Values are mostly sound (attentive_proactive for glowing crew mentions), but the seat-focused negative review with no crew mention was labeled 'inattentive_robotic', an unwarranted inference where the text is silent on crew, lowering groundedness.

per_column.name: food_quality_issue_type
per_column.rationale: A specific typology of food problems gives a genuine axis to diagnose dissatisfaction drivers. Sampled values are well grounded: 'no_issue' correctly applied to positive/silent food rows, matching source text.

per_column.name: special_meal_service_failure
per_column.rationale: A narrow boolean (35 true) targeting special-meal failures; useful but a near-constant, niche flag with limited leverage. Sampled 'False' values are correctly assigned where no special meal is mentioned.

per_column.name: service_amenity_reduction
per_column.rationale: Graded scale of amenity cuts offers a useful comparative axis for perceived degradation. Sampled 'no_reduction' values align with texts that mention no cutbacks; reasonable defaulting for silent rows.

per_column.name: cabin_class_value_gap
per_column.rationale: Excellent axis for the query: whether the class delivered value directly speaks to value-for-money and recommendation. Most samples sound (premium_underdelivered, economy_exceeded_expectations), but 'value_met' assigned to a very short positive economy note is a stretch, and the label requires class context not always present, slightly weakening groundedness.

per_column.name: service_consistency_decline
per_column.rationale: Boolean capturing perceived decline/inconsistency is relevant to the improvement query, though it partially overlaps with the crew-quality axis. Sampled 'False' values match texts that report consistent good service.

per_column.name: loyalty_program_friction
per_column.rationale: A niche boolean (33 true) about loyalty/status friction; only marginally connected to the general rating/recommendation query and near-constant. Sampled 'False' values are correctly assigned where no loyalty program is mentioned.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively provide several genuinely useful analytical axes (crew service quality, food issue types, class value gap, amenity reduction) that map well onto diagnosing why passengers do not recommend the airline and where improvement is possible. A couple of columns (special_meal_service_failure, loyalty_program_friction) are narrow near-constant booleans with limited leverage. Groundedness is generally solid, with sampled values reading soundly from source text; the main weaknesses are over-confident inferences on silent rows for crew quality (labeling a seat-only complaint as 'inattentive_robotic') and class-value labels where class context is thin.
